title: Safer bundles and a shorter path to first use
summary: This release fixes a path-escape defect found by running Launch GitHub Project against its own repository, then turns that failure into reusable release checks and a deterministic GitHub Release-page workflow.
highlights: Rejects file and directory symlinks and non-regular entries before the release bundler reads them; see the [reproduction, root cause and remaining boundary](https://github.com/weike-zhang/launch-github-project/blob/v0.1.2/examples/self-audit-bundle-safety.md).
Treats tracked symlinks as public-surface blockers and adds regression coverage for file and directory path escape.
Reduces the end-user quick start to install plus invoke; maintainer gates now stay in the installation guide.
Adds adoption-and-trust guidance that separates discovery, first success, direct proof, repeat use, contribution and popularity.
Generates GitHub Release pages from structured evidence and rejects stale pages or mismatched plugin versions.
verification: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — all release-tool regression tests passed.
`python3 evals/validate_fixtures.py` — all fixture-integrity scenarios passed; this is not a model-quality score.
Local link, redacted secret and strict public-surface checks completed with no findings.
The deterministic ZIP was opened, listed and extracted successfully before upload.
compatibility: Skills CLI repository discovery is verified for the `launch-github-project` Skill.
The bundled scripts are verified with Python 3.12 in GitHub Actions.
Other Agent Skills hosts remain unverified unless listed separately.
limitations: Symlink rejection closes the documented static path-escape case; it is not a general sandbox and does not eliminate concurrent file-replacement races.
Automated checks do not prove asset ownership, user adoption or unsigned remote rendering.
Creating a GitHub Release, uploading assets and changing repository metadata still require explicit remote authorization.
